models.AuditEvent.description: One recorded action in a network's audit log

changes.description:
Changes maps each changed field to {"from": old, "to": new}, or to
{"changed": true} for redacted fields. Over the size cap it is
{"_truncated": true, "fields": [names]}, without fields when the names
alone are too long. It is null when the action records no changes.

request_id.description: RequestID correlates the event with request logs. Clients may set it.

id.description: ID is the user's ID or the API key's (network password's) ID.

name.description:
Name is a snapshot taken when the event was recorded: the user's email
or the API key's name. It is null when unknown, such as for unnamed keys.
Name is a snapshot taken when the event was recorded, or null.

models.ConnectPlayerRequest.description: Request to connect a player. Set exactly one of server_id, server_name, server_group_id, server_group_name and persistent_server_id.

selection_mode.description: How to pick a server of a group: RANDOM (default); MIN_PLAYERS or MAX_PLAYERS by reported player count; FIRST, the lowest numerical ID. Validated for every target, but only group targets use it: an unknown value is a 400.

server_name.description: Cloud server name, matched case-insensitively: a persistent server's name, or "<group>-<numerical_id>". This is the name the cloud gives the server, not the name a proxy registered it under. A name of both a persistent server and a group server is a 409.

result.description: How the connect ended. Older clients read message instead: NO_SERVER_AVAILABLE and SERVER_NOT_FOUND both have the message "Target server not found".

server_name.description: Cloud name of the server the player was last sent to; absent when no server was available

models.ConnectResult.description: How a connect ended. SUCCESS: the proxy sent the player to the server. ALREADY_CONNECTED: the player already is on it. NO_SERVER_AVAILABLE: the target exists, but has no server a player can join right now, so nothing was sent; an unknown target is a 404 instead. SERVER_NOT_FOUND: the proxy does not know the server, typically because it has not registered it yet. FAILED: the proxy could not send the player.

BearerAuth.description: JWT sent in Authorization: Bearer <token>. Access depends on the token's network membership and permissions. The admin endpoint requires admin claims.

NetworkCredential.description: Network password or signed JWT. Password authentication also requires X-Network-ID and grants full access to that network, except the audit log. JWT permissions still apply.
NetworkCredential.name: X-Network-Credential

NetworkJWT.description: Signed JWT with admin claims. Network passwords cannot authorize admin operations.
NetworkJWT.name: X-Network-Credential

info.description: Manage Minecraft networks, server groups, persistent servers, players, and plugins. Authenticate with Authorization: Bearer <JWT> or X-Network-Credential: <network password or JWT>. Bearer authentication takes precedence when both headers are supplied. Network-scoped operations also require X-Network-ID. JWT permissions and network membership restrict access; network passwords grant full access to their network, except that they cannot read the audit log. Registration requires an existing credential; password authentication also requires its existing network ID. The admin endpoint requires an admin JWT. Credential verification accepts credentials in the request body without authentication headers.

get.description: List all networks. Requires admin access.

Lists the network's audit events, newest first. Requires the audit_log:read permission, which covers every event in the network regardless of the caller's other permissions. API keys (network passwords) cannot read the audit log. To get the next page, pass next_cursor as cursor with the same filters.

delete.description: Delete the network's shared public key, so the next serverhost to start registers its key again. Refused with 409 while the network stores secrets, because they are encrypted with this key; delete them first. Serverhosts keep their copy of the private key and re-register it on their next start, so this does not rotate the key unless the private key is also removed from every serverhost.
